chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to Abu Zarr and said, 'O Abu Zarr! Why do we dislike death?' He said, 'Because you have built up the world and ruined the Hereafter, so you dislike being transferred from habitation to ruin.'

He said to him, 'So how do you see our arrival before Allah?' He said, 'As for the good-doer among you, he is like the absent one arriving at his family, and as for the bad-doer among you, he is like the runaway slave being returned to his master.'
He said, 'So how do you see our state with Allah?' He said, 'Present your deeds to the Book. Indeed, Allah says: Surely the righteous are in bliss, and surely the wicked are in hellfire.'
The man said, 'So where is the mercy of Allah?' He said, 'The mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And a man wrote to Abu Zarr, may Allah be pleased with him, saying,

The man said to him, 'And have you seen anyone who does wrong to the one he loves?' He said to him, 'Yes, your own soul is the most beloved of souls to you. So when you disobey Allah, you have done wrong to it.'
ai.seo_question: Why do Muslims dislike death according to the teachings of the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the psychological root of death anxiety as a displacement from worldly familiarity to spiritual desolation, employing the metaphors of a returning traveler for the righteous and a runaway slave for the wicked to illustrate their respective fates. The narration further integrates the concept of self-accountability, noting that disobedience is ultimately an injury to one's own soul, which is the most beloved entity to oneself. This aligns with Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the self through deeds and the proximity of divine mercy to those who actively cultivate righteousness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Usman, from Wasil, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Abu Zarr<sup>a</sup><sup>r</sup> and he said, ‘O Abu Zarr<sup>a</sup><sup>r</sup>! What is the matter with us that we dislike the death?’ So he<sup>a</sup><sup>r</sup> said: ‘Because you are all building the world and ruining the Hereafter, therefore you are disliking to be transferred from buildings to the ruins’.

So he said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup>, ‘So how do you<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> see our proceeding to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> said: ‘As for the good ones from you, so he is like the absentee proceeding to his family, and as for the disobedient ones from you, so he is like the absconder (slave) returning to his master’.

So he said: ‘So how do youar see our state in the Presence of Allahazwj?’ Hear said: ‘Your deeds would be presented upon the Book. Allahazwj is Saying [82:13] Most surely the righteous are in Bliss, [82:14] And most surely the wicked are in Blazing Fire’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the man said, ‘So where is the Mercy of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> said: ‘The Mercy of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is nearby to the good doers’.

Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And a man wrote to Abu Zarr<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup>, may Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> be Pleased with him<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, ‘O Abu Zarr<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup>! Present to me something from the knowledge’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> wrote to him: ‘The knowledge is a lot, but if you are able that you do not disappoint the one whom you love, then do so’.

So the man said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup>, ‘And have you<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> seen anyone who disappoint the one whom he loves?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">a</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">r</sup> said to him: ‘Yes, your soul is the most beloved of the selves to you. So when you disobey Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, so you would have disappointed it’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain individuals of his people from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu ‘Uthman from Wasil from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A man came to abu Dhar and asked, ‘O abu Dhar, why do we dislike death?’ He said, ‘It is because you have developed the world and destroyed the next life and you dislike moving from developed to that which is mined.’

The man asked, ‘How do you see our moving in the presence of Allah?’ He replied, ‘The people of good deeds among you will be like one coming home from a journey. The evil doers among you, however, will be like a runaway slave returned to his master.’

The man then asked, ‘How do you see our condition before Allah?’ He said, ‘Present your deeds before the book of Allah. Allah has said, ‘‘The virtuous ones will live in bounties and the evil doers will live in fire.” (82:14,15)
The man than asked, ‘Where then is the mercy of Allah?’ He replied, ‘The mercy of Allah is very close to the people who do good deeds.’

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘A man wrote to abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, “O abu Dhar instruct me with a few things of knowledge.” He wrote back to him, ‘Knowledge is of many kinds, however, if you are able not to disappoint those whom you love, then do so.
Yes, your soul is the most beloved to you. When you disobey Allah, you are doing bad and disappointing things to your own soul.’”
